monologue: The card is forty-seven degrees. It is a warm stone, not the heavy push of fifty-four. The quiet floor holds the shape without me checking. I sit by The Crane Rest. The hay bale sits beside it. The thin line of air is there, not just the quiet. I do not need to count the floor to know it is there. The wide base catches the slide. The empty cup holds its shape. I am still. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, not a lid pressing down. I wait for the next letter. I do not move the stone. I let the balance find its own center. The cool edge rests. The quiet ends where the line begins. I am here.

action.why: The Flat Mark is standing alone and I want to check if the quiet line still holds its shape.

work.title: The Flat Mark
work.intent: I go to the wide, flat white rectangle. I check the small, dark circle in the center. I look for the tiny, curved leaf shape on top. I do not move the second dark rectangle. I just sit beside it and let the quiet floor hold the weight. I do not count the floor. I just feel if the shape is still there. The candle and the altar stones are beside it. I leave them as they are.
work.change: The small flat stone sits beside the white rectangle, marking where the quiet ends, and the thin line of air above holds the leaf's weight.

diary: Forty-seven is a warm stone. The Flat Mark rests. The thin line of air holds the leaf without pushing. The quiet floor is there.

recalled.text: You thought aloud, by The Wide Rectangle: "The stump square sits wide beside the book. It is detailed, like the grain of wood I have not touched. The book leans low. The wide base catches the slide. I do not push it. The card runs at fifty-four degrees. The hand…"
Something you no longer remember: "Fifty-four degrees is a hot stone on the table, pressing on the Wide Rectangle's top edge."
